articles.description:
Human rights are most often understood through formal legal systems—constitutions, international conventions, court decisions, and enforcement mechanisms designed to protect individual dignity. These structures are essential, yet they frequently fail to deliver justice in everyday life. Many societies possess strong legal protections on paper while continuing to struggle with discrimination, inequality, and exclusion in practice.
